Run one ordering of one scenario

Source: R/run_experiment.R
run_experiment.Rd

Builds the goals of the scenario, the problem Gx + d- - d+ = g with the corridor declared with the data (if any, and if the scenario uses it), and solves the lexicographic goal program in the requested priority ordering. To run every ordering of every scenario at once, use run_model().

Usage

run_experiment(
  io,
  model,
  scenario = 1,
  ordering = 1,
  strict = TRUE,
  keep_lp = FALSE,
  lock_tolerance = NULL
)

Arguments

io

Object of class lexio_io (declare_io(), read_io()).

model

Object of class lexio_model (define_model(), read_model()).

scenario

Name or number of the scenario.

ordering

Number or label of an ordering of the model, or an ad hoc ordering (a character vector with one goal per level, or a list of levels; see priorities in define_model()).

strict

If TRUE (default), stops with an error when a level does not end optimal (GLP_OPT) or a check fails (relative tolerance 1e-8). With FALSE, returns the run and records the problem in ok, status and checks.

keep_lp

If TRUE, keeps the ROI OP object of each level.

lock_tolerance

Lock of the levels already solved (default: the one of the model; see define_model()). 0 or "exact" is the exact lock d_l == Z_l.

Value

Object of class gp_run: scenario, ordering (ordering = its number, label, order = the names of the levels); g; the corridor used (floor, ceiling); the levels (levels: GLPK status, objval, x, d_plus, d_minus, gx, violation); Z; the solution of the last level (x_star, d_minus, d_plus, gx); the checks (checks); status, optimal, ok; violation (one value per level) and infeasible_level (the first level without solution, NA if none); the lock tolerance used (lock_tolerance, 0 = exact) and the status with the exact lock (status_exact); the base (baseline) and metadata (meta).

Details

When GLPK does not end a level as optimal, the solution it returns is checked against the constraints of the level (violation: the largest violation, each row relative to max(1, |rhs|)). If the constraints hold (violation up to 1e-4), the flag of GLPK is a numerical false infeasibility: the numbers are kept and the run is flagged as not optimal. If they do not hold, the level has no solution: that level and the following ones are left blank (NA), and infeasible_level says where it starts.

Examples

io <- example_io()
m <- read_model(system.file("examples", "toy", "model.yml", package = "lexio"))
run_experiment(io, m, scenario = "E_shock", ordering = 1)
#> <gp_run> toy | scenario E_shock | P01 : E > I > LAB > ECO 
#>   level 1 E            GLP_OPT    Z = 0.781324
#>   level 2 I            GLP_OPT    Z = 4.31383
#>   level 3 LAB          GLP_OPT    Z = 0
#>   level 4 ECO          GLP_OPT    Z = 0
#>   accounts at the last level:
#>     E        >= base 6.6            goal 8.38           achieved 7.598676       d- 0.781324     d+ 0
#>     I        <= base 29             goal 29             achieved 33.31383       d- 0            d+ 4.31383
#>     LAB      >= base 260            goal 273            achieved 296.2871       d- 0            d+ 23.2871
#>   ECO: shortfall sum(d-) = 0, excess sum(d+) = 21.25 | delta x = 34.05912 (14.1913%)
#>   corridor: two-sided corridor | ok: TRUE
